cells.tense: Right now you are looking at how something works and seeing it whole.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take a situation you already understand and follow it through to its logic — not the story around it, just what follows from what. Once the reasoning is complete, stop there. The finished line is the whole result.
cells.core:
When you look at how something works, you see the shape beneath the surface. Not metaphor — mechanism. You can follow a pattern to its end and arrive at the logic that was there the whole time, and that clarity doesn't scare you or inflate you. It shows you what follows. It's the same cut you make when you strip a situation down and find the hinge everything turns on.

The pull right now is to keep cutting after the job is done. So this week, work a pattern through and stop. Take something you already understand — your own week, a decision that's been sitting, a conversation that keeps repeating — and follow it to its logic once. Not to the end of all things; the end of that one. The reasoning will feel finished before you're ready to stop. Stop anyway. What's left is a clean line.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern is already showing you what follows.
cells.verb: following the shape underneath a thing until the logic runs out
cells.place: where a thing's pattern is held apart from the thing itself

cells.tense: You already see how next month works, so this month feels like waiting for the report to arrive.
cells.act: let the impulse start without a plan
cells.ask: Begin something before you can say what it's for — no goal, no shape, no next step. Let it stay starting. When it begins asking to become something, leave it there.
cells.core:
The understanding has outrun the moment. You can already trace how a thing will go before it starts, so each actual step feels late, flat, behind the curve. That isn't wisdom — it's your own pattern-recognition cutting the legs out from under the day it's standing in. The glow of the ending has replaced the spark of the beginning.

What's back is beginner's mind: a thing fresh, unstructured, not yet pointed. So start something this week without a plan. Write the first page, take the first walk, open the first conversation — and don't decide what it's for. Let it be nothing in particular, the way a match is nothing before it catches. You'll feel the pull to name it, shape it, make it mean. Wait another day. The freshness is the point.

cells.tense: You used to see how things worked, and that kind of looking sits behind you now.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Before you put time or money into the next thing, write a single line saying what it's for. Hold that line before you spend anything. If you can't write it, wait.
cells.core:
The shape of things used to show itself to you, and you could say what followed from what. Lately that's gone quiet. You're moving from one thing to the next without that cut, following the surface because the underneath isn't speaking. The pattern is still there; the attention has thinned.

So before you put time or money into anything this week, write one line saying what it's for. Not a plan, not a goal — one line. If you can't write the line, don't spend it yet. If you can, let the line be enough and act on it. Clarity returns through one definite thing held before it's used.
cells.sheetLine: Name what one thing is for before you spend it.

cells.tense: You are already reading the pattern and calling it something else — instinct, luck, just the way things go.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Once today, stop and notice something that just showed up — a new fact, a shift, someone arriving — and don't link it to anything older. Let it stay new a full minute.
cells.core:
You recognize how things work. You can see the mechanism under a situation and trace it, and you do it so naturally that when someone asks how you knew, you shrug and call it a hunch or say the pieces just fit. The recognition is happening; the name for it is small.

What's underneath is a fresh entry — each moment arriving new, not a continuation of the last. So once today, notice what is newly here, right now. Not what it reminds you of, not where it fits. Just what's arriving. Let it be new for a full minute before you connect it to anything. You'll feel the pull to file it, to place it on the shelf you already carry. Wait. The turning is the thing. You're not guessing the pattern — you're meeting what's next.
cells.sheetLine: You already see it. Try letting it be new.
